analysis.event: NanoViricides announced the start of a Phase II clinical trial of NV-387 as a treatment for Monkeypox (MPox) virus infection, with enrollment of the first patients in the DRC. The trial is conducted by NanoViricides, Inc.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial plans to enroll a further 50 patients in the first half of 2026 for interim efficacy analysis. No specific case counts, death counts, or risk levels were reported in the supplied evidence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial is ongoing, with the first 50 patients randomized and no new safety concerns identified. The trial's design includes an adaptive, international, multi-center, randomized, open-label, interventional, parallel group structure.

analysis.brief_en: NanoViricides, Inc. has announced the initiation of a Phase II clinical trial for its novel antiviral drug NV-387, aimed at treating Monkeypox (MPox) virus infection. The trial began on September 23, 2026, with the enrollment of the first patients in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The trial is designed as an adaptive, international, multi-center, randomized, open-label, interventional, parallel group study to evaluate the drug's efficacy and safety in patients with clinical signs of mpox disease and laboratory-confirmed or presumptive MPXV infection. As of January 2026, the Data Safety and Monitoring Board (DSMB) did not identify any new safety concerns after the first 50 patients were randomized. The trial plans to enroll an additional 50 patients in the first half of 2026 for interim efficacy analysis. No specific case counts, death counts, or risk levels were reported in the supplied evidence. The trial is part of NanoViricides' broader efforts to develop treatments for infectious diseases, including mpox.

title: More than a third of positive tests for mpox may have been false diagnoses

analysis.time: The study was conducted between April 2024 and April 2026, with the findings published on 22 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on four cities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC): Goma, Kamituga, Kinshasa, and Uvira. It involved PCR testing for mpox in these areas.
analysis.event: An international team led by the University of Geneva (UNIGE) found that 35% of PCR-positive mpox tests in the DRC may have been false diagnoses due to environmental contamination of samples.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study highlights the potential for significant false-positive diagnoses in mpox testing, which could lead to unnecessary overtreatment, hospitalisation, or quarantine for individuals without actual infection. This has implications for public health resource allocation and the accuracy of outbreak surveillance.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study suggests adjusting the PCR positivity threshold to reduce false positives and improve diagnostic accuracy. It also emphasizes the need for better lab staff training in low-resource settings to identify such anomalies in real time.

analysis.brief_en: A study led by the University of Geneva (UNIGE) and conducted in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) between April 2024 and April 2026 found that 35% of PCR-positive mpox tests may have been false diagnoses due to environmental contamination. The research, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, revealed that mpox DNA can persist on surfaces and in the air of treatment centers, leading to incorrect results when testing other patients. This finding has significant implications for public health, as it could result in unnecessary hospitalization, quarantine, or treatment for individuals without actual infection. The study recommends lowering the PCR positivity threshold to reduce false positives without increasing false negatives, and improving lab staff training in low-resource settings to detect such anomalies promptly. The WHO declared the mpox outbreak in the DRC a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024, underscoring the importance of accurate diagnosis for effective public health measures.

source_language_evidence.location_and_population: # 兔模型用于MPXV Clade Ib与IIb.A.2.1致病性比较研究解读 ## 研究背景与问题 Mpox(猴痘)是由正痘病毒属(Orthopoxvirus)病原体引起的人畜共患疾病,近年来已成为日益重要的全球公共卫生问题。该疾病于1970年在刚果民主共和国首次被发现,此后数十年间主要局限于中非和西非地区,感染主要与接触这些地区感染的啮齿动物有关。然而,2022年Mpox发生全球传播,成为非洲以外报告的最大规模流行,促使世界卫生组织(WHO)于2022年7月23日至2023年5月10日宣布其为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件。与此前通常与疫区旅行史或动物接触相关的感染不同,2022年流行与个体间的性接触相关。2024年,中非和东非报告的Mpox病例再次增加,WHO于2024年8月14日第二次宣布国际关注的突发公共卫生事件。

source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: **病毒脱落与器官嗜性:** MPXV DNA仅在感染后第8和10天于两组各2/5兔的口腔拭子中检出;而鼻拭子中的病毒DNA从第4天即可检出并持续至第14天,在第8和10天时所有兔鼻拭子均为阳性。从第8天的鼻拭子样本(PCR循环阈值(Ct)范围21至34)和皮肤结痂样本(Ct范围17至36)中成功分离出病毒。第14天收集的睾丸样本中,Clade Ib组4/5和Clade IIb.A.2.1组4/5检测到病毒DNA,并成功分离出病毒。此外,Clade Ib和IIb.A.2.1组各有1只兔肺样本、Clade Ib组3只兔肝和脾样本检出病毒DNA,但未能分离到病毒;淋巴结样本均为阴性。

analysis.time: The cases were reported last Friday, with health officials now strengthening surveillance and response measures across the province. The publication date is 22 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Gauteng province, South Africa. The health department is focusing on the province's population and health districts.
analysis.event: Gauteng Health has confirmed three cases of Mpox and is preparing to respond to the outbreak. The National Institute For Communicable Diseases (NICD) reported the cases, and health officials are strengthening surveillance and response measures.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Three confirmed cases of Mpox have been reported. Mpox vaccines are available in stock with 586 doses currently in dedicated freezers at regional pharmacies. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Outbreak response teams are active across all five health districts, with specialist teams monitoring suspected and confirmed cases. analysis.brief_en: Gauteng Health has confirmed three cases of Mpox, prompting the province's health department to prepare for an outbreak response. The National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) reported the cases last Friday, and health officials are now strengthening surveillance and response measures across the province. Mpox vaccines are available in stock, with 586 doses currently stored in dedicated freezers at regional pharmacies. These vaccines require special cold-chain storage, and clinics can request doses when there is an identified need. The department has activated outbreak response teams in all five health districts, with specialist teams monitoring suspected and confirmed cases. Daily monitoring of cases is conducted through the notifiable medical conditions surveillance system, and wastewater surveillance is also being used as an early warning mechanism. Residents are urged to remain vigilant and recognize the signs and symptoms of Mpox to seek medical care early. The department is also in communication with the national health authorities to ensure additional vaccine doses can be accessed if necessary.
